programme.title: The Silence of the Lambs
programme.desc: Multi-Oscar-winning thriller about a trainee female FBI agent who is seconded to the hunt for a horrific serial killer. For insight into the workings of his diseased mind she turns to the psychotic yet urbane Dr Hannibal 'the Cannibal' Lecter, with whom she forms a compelling and dangerous relationship.

programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: A look back at the life of the Oscar-winning actor Sir Anthony Hopkins. In interviews conducted with the BBC over the course of his career he discusses his approach to acting, his years as a hell-raiser, and the famous films and roles that helped make him a star.

programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: Celia Imrie tells the story of Glenda Jackson, one of Britain's greatest-ever acting talents and a double Oscar winner, who famously turned her back on her hugely successful screen career to pursue a life in politics.

programme.title: How to Get Ahead
programme.desc: Stephen Smith explores Renaissance Florence under the reign of Grand Duke Cosimo Medici. Cosimo's fledgling court prized the finer things in life and some of the greatest painters, sculptors and craftsmen in world history came to serve the Grand Duke. However, successful courtiers had to have brains as well as brawn. The canniest of them looked to theorists like Niccolò Machiavelli for underhand ways to get ahead, whilst enlightened polymaths turned their minds to the heavens, and to ice cream.

programme.title: Whitney at the BBC
programme.desc: A reflection on Whitney Houston's best performances at the BBC celebrates the hit songs of one of the most successful artists in the world. Taking a sonic trip through the star's career, from the 1985 hit 'Saving all My Love for you', all the way through the 80s, 90s and 00s, this selection of songs educates on the artist's appeal to audiences everywhere and her ability to gain longstanding fans across multiple decades. It also reflects on why the singer's untimely death was such a deep loss.

programme.title: Whitney Houston: The Concert for a New South Africa (Durban)
programme.desc: In 1994, Whitney Houston took the stage in Durban, South Africa, making her the first major Western musician to visit the newly unified, post-apartheid nation following President Nelson Mandela's winning election. More than a concert, it was a celebration of freedom, hope, and unity. Whitney's powerhouse voice and emotional delivery brought joy and inspiration to a country newly liberated.

programme.title: Planet Earth III
programme.desc: Exploring astonishing wild places and the most spectacular moments from the series. In the planet's oldest desert, a pair of ostriches raise their family in the searing heat to keep them safe from predators, but time is ticking.

programme.title: Life on Air: David Attenborough's 50 Years in Television
programme.desc: David Attenborough is one of Britain's best-known TV personalities, having presented programmes - usually about animals or natural history - for decades. Actor Michael Palin presents this special that takes a look back at the TV legend's career, using classic clips, outtakes and anecdotes to highlight Attenborough's work. `Life on Air' also interviews Attenborough and some key figures in his life, including his brother, actor Richard Attenborough. David also welcomes viewers into his home and on the set as he works on one of his programmes.

programme.title: Life on Earth
programme.desc: The story of life, from the first primitive cells to the plants and animals that now live around us. David Attenborough goes on a world journey looking at the incredible variety of living things and fossils which throw light on the ancestry of life.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: A tigress is chosen to found a new dynasty. Airlifted from her home in an Indian park to life in a new reserve, Baghani the tigress must fight with leopards for territory and learn to hunt dangerous wild boar. Also released is Rajore, a young male.

programme.title: The Magic of Dance
programme.desc: In the 20th century, Sergei Diaghilev brought the Ballets Russes to live and work in Western Europe. Margot Fonteyn visits Tchaikovsky's house near Moscow and talks to Marie Rambert about Diaghilev.

programme.title: Omnibus
programme.desc: An Omnibus special, first broadcast in 1995, shortly after the death of Ginger Rogers. The film looks at how the legendary Fred and Ginger musicals were made and features anecdotes from Rogers and clips from Astaire's last television interview.

programme.title: Puttin' on the Ritz: The Genius of Fred Astaire
programme.desc: A short compilation of clips from Fred Astaire's days at the RKO studio, where he formed an unforgettable partnership with Ginger Rogers.

programme.title: Dance Passion Swansea
programme.desc: Dancers of all kinds take over Swansea's streets, landmarks, parks and beaches to showcase the city, explore what home means and celebrate the life-enhancing joy of dance. There are solos, duets and ensembles. From ballet, Latin and contemporary to ballroom, breaking, traditional clog and Welsh folk dance. Locations range from Mumbles Pier and skateboard park to Swansea Bay and the dunes, beaches and bays of the Gower peninsula.

programme.title: Election 26
programme.desc: Laura Kuenssberg is your guide as the results of this year's council elections in England begin to flood in. Reeta Chakrabarti will crunch the numbers at her giant screen, and Professor Sir John Curtice will be on hand to offer his psephological knowledge and insight. BBC regional political editors will be at the most important counts, and representatives of the main political parties will give their reaction to the emerging political landscape.
